note: Scripted DYNAMIC obstacles for sim/worlds/farmguard_field.sdf (Gazebo SDF <actor> elements, per-actor <script><trajectory> keyframes -- no runtime randomness, so 'fixed seed' is trivial here: these waypoints ARE the deterministic path, committed as data). Matches MVP scope: 2-3 birds, not a flock (docs/SPEC.md, CLAUDE.md). Trajectory style (piecewise-linear waypoints: t_s, x_m, y_m, z_m) intentionally mirrors sim/spike/scenario_default.json's bird scripting for consistency across the project, though the concrete numbers differ because this world's field (75x60m, config/field_polygon.json) is a different size than the spike's standalone clip field.
coordinate_frame: local ENU meters (x=East, y=North, z=Up), origin = config/field_polygon.json home_lat/home_lon.
generator: scripts/gen_farm_world.py reads this file and emits the matching <actor> blocks in sim/worlds/farmguard_field.sdf. Each bird's waypoint list is a there-and-back path (last waypoint == first waypoint's position) so SDF's <loop>true</loop> replays seamlessly with no teleport jump between cycles.
sdf_actor_note: Gazebo actors have a visual (here: a small flat-colored sphere, no mesh/skin needed) and move along the scripted trajectory automatically once auto_start=true -- no plugin required (gz-sim Harmonic). Actors do not physically collide in gz-sim's actor system (this is a gz-sim limitation, not a SwathKeeper choice) -- they exist for the future NDVI-camera-based detection/avoidance loop (Week 3-4), not for Gazebo physics collision.

birds.note: south<->north sweep at x=20 (between orchard rows 0 and 1), mid-low altitude (8m AGL, 7m below the 15m mission altitude).
east<->west sweep at y=30 (mid-field), altitude 11m AGL (4m below mission altitude) -- crosses all 3 orchard rows.

diagonal SW<->NE sweep, low altitude (6m AGL, closest to canopy height of the 3 birds -- the most safety-relevant trajectory for future avoidance work since it's nearest the tree obstacles' height band).
